1936.us: Franklin Roosevelt won re-election in a landslide in November, carrying 46 of the 48 states.
1936.latam: Roosevelt opened the Inter-American Conference for the Maintenance of Peace in Buenos Aires in December, where American republics pledged to consult on threats to peace.
1936.europe: Germany remilitarised the Rhineland in March, and in July a military uprising began the Spanish Civil War.
1936.russia: In August the first Moscow show trial sentenced Zinoviev and Kamenev to death; in December Stalin’s new Soviet constitution was adopted.
1936.mideast: Farouk became King of Egypt in April, and in August the Anglo-Egyptian Treaty set terms for British troops to stay near the Suez Canal.
1936.africa: Italian troops took Addis Ababa in May; in June the exiled Emperor Haile Selassie appealed to the League of Nations in Geneva.
1936.india: Peasant leaders founded the All India Kisan Sabha at Lucknow in April, with Swami Sahajanand Saraswati as its president.
1936.china: In December, in the Xi’an Incident, Marshal Zhang Xueliang detained Chiang Kai-shek to push him into a united front against Japan.

1911.us: The Supreme Court ordered Standard Oil broken up in May; in March the Triangle fire killed 146 garment workers in New York.
1911.latam: Revolution forced Mexico’s Porfirio Díaz to resign in May and go into exile; Francisco Madero won the presidency in October.
1911.europe: Germany sent the gunboat Panther to Agadir in July, setting off a crisis with France; Britain’s Parliament Act curbed the House of Lords.
1911.russia: Prime Minister Pyotr Stolypin was shot at the Kiev opera house in September and died four days later.
1911.mideast: Italy declared war on the Ottoman Empire in September and invaded Libya; in November an Italian pilot dropped the first bombs from a plane.
1911.africa: The new Union of South Africa passed the Mines and Works Act, reserving skilled mining jobs for white workers.
1911.india: At the Delhi Durbar in December, George V announced the capital would move from Calcutta to Delhi and reversed the partition of Bengal.
1911.china: The Wuchang Uprising in October began the revolution against the Qing dynasty; in December Sun Yat-sen was elected provisional president.

2013.us: From June, leaks by contractor Edward Snowden revealed mass surveillance by the National Security Agency.
2013.latam: Venezuela’s Hugo Chávez died in March, and Argentina’s Jorge Bergoglio became Pope Francis, the first pope from the Americas.
2013.europe: Croatia joined the European Union on 1 July as its 28th member state.
2013.russia: A meteor exploded over Chelyabinsk in February, injuring about 1,500 people, mostly from broken glass.
2013.mideast: Egypt’s army removed President Mohamed Morsi in July, a year after he became the country’s first freely elected president.
2013.africa: Nelson Mandela, South Africa’s first Black president, died in December at 95.
2013.india: Bangladesh’s Rana Plaza collapse killed 1,134 in April, and in November India launched its Mars Orbiter Mission.
2013.china: Xi Jinping became China’s president in March and in September proposed a Silk Road Economic Belt, the start of the Belt and Road.
